summary: context-mode ships an offline benchmark suite (bench/run.mjs, 66 scenarios) with a committed results file, from which the README's 99.4% median byte saving recomputes (36 rows with 10 KB or more of raw output); these are byte counts on fixtures with tokens estimated as bytes / 4, not model runs. Live A/B runs in Claude Code with claude-sonnet-5-5 (scripts and committed aggregates; rerunning needs the `claude` CLI and paid model calls) found v2 cut the median tool_result bytes on large tasks by 84% (734.5 vs 4,694.5) with 12 of 12 large-task sessions passing in every arm, while session tokens were 5.7% worse than no plugin on small tasks and 19.6% worse on large ones; a later run put v2's session tokens 3.8% below no plugin on large tasks and 5.6% above on small ones. A paired cost study with committed run files and an analysis script found the open-source plugin cost more than Claude Code alone on six short tasks (v1 34.6% more, v2 2.2% more) and the hosted Context Mode Gateway's published rows 24.5% less, and the repo's own check of 13 numbers from the README's Try It section (commit a92cf6a7, measured on v1) found that 2 hold and 11 differ.
result_focus_note: manual classification of published_results: outcome = does the tool do its job; engineering = speed of the software itself
